fields.description:
## Context

The root tree holds 6,008 flat ticket directories and is 270 KB; every commit re-emits the WHOLE
root tree, so tree bytes are ~95% of the blobless pack. Sharding the flat namespace shrinks the
per-commit root-tree object so each re-emission is far smaller — a durable structural reduction of
the tree churn that dominates the pack, complementing S1 (historical) and W1 (write-rate).

## Scope

Shard the flat `tickets/<id>` layout into a fan-out namespace (target: `tickets/<first-two-hex>/<id>`)
so a mutation re-emits only a small shard subtree plus a small top-level tree, not a 270 KB flat
root. Preserve ticket resolution (alias/short-id/full-id), event replay, and reconcile behavior.
Requires a migration path for existing ticket paths.

## Out of scope

The history reclaim (S1), write-batching (W1), and the live shared-store cutover. This is the
on-disk tree LAYOUT only. The live `.tickets-tracker` migration/cutover sequencing is an operator
decision and will not be performed by this task.

## Implementation Plan

1. Add a single ticket-layout helper that derives canonical sharded ticket directories, resolves
   legacy flat directories during the expand phase, iterates both layouts deterministically, and
   exposes store-relative paths for git staging.
2. Move the write path (`stage_event`/append/txn-style writers) to publish new events under the
   sharded path while still reading existing flat paths until the migration has converged.
3. Update replay, resolver, graph, lifecycle, compaction/fsck/sidecar readers, and reconciler-local
   ticket lookups to route through the shared helper instead of composing `tracker/<id>` directly.
4. Add an idempotent ensure-registry unit that migrates existing flat ticket directories into the
   sharded namespace on throwaway stores, tree-checks before committing, preserves all directory
   names/event bytes, refuses ambiguous collisions, and is safe to re-run.
5. Prove the behavior with RED-first fixture tests: writer/tree-byte reduction, migration identity
   preservation, resolver/replay compatibility, and reconvergence/merge-as-union preservation.

## Test Plan / Acceptance Evidence

- Unit/store test creates many fixture tickets, mutates one, and compares git tree object bytes for
  the flat layout vs the sharded layout to prove per-commit root-tree churn drops substantially.
- Migration test creates a legacy flat fixture, runs only the new ensure unit, asserts every ticket
  identity (full id, alias, short id) resolves to the same state afterward and a second run is a no-op.
- Existing resolver/replay tests plus targeted compatibility tests prove alias, short-id, full-id, and
  event replay are unchanged across mixed flat+sharded stores.
- Reconvergence fixture with two clones writing different ticket shards proves merge-as-union behavior
  preserves both sides after sharding.

## Portability

Pure store-layout change with an in-process, idempotent ensure-registry migration; no dependence on
any single CI provider. Migration validation is confined to fixture/throwaway stores; no live-store
cutover is performed.
